text:
alex.h: proposing we switch canary splitting for model rollout to consistent-hash based routing rather than header-percentage. reasons: stable user experience, easier analytics by user_id, avoids sticky cookie pain

maria.k: ooo interesting. how do you plan to surface the hash key in the console? we need devs to be able to pick between user_id / session_id / header

jamal.r: consistent-hash is great but watch out for retries and proxies altering headers. if the key is `x-session-id` and some clients rewrite it, skew happens.

alex.h: agreed. suggested default: `hash_key = user_id || x-session-id || x-redwood-entropy` (first available). console should show the chosen key and a sample distribution.

infra-bot: deploy: canary model-v2 -> 10% (consistent-hash) by alex.h at 2025-10-11T14:02:03Z :rocket:

taylor.p: +1 but we still need an override path for QA and partners. propose `x-redwood-canary-override: model-v2` allowlist controlled in routing policy (auth + audit).

maria.k: override header is fine but add rate limits + telemetry label `override:true`. otherwise analytics will be polluted.

jamal.r: on telemetry, we should emit `routing.key`, `routing.hash_bucket`, and `routing.variant` to span tags. that way we can aggregate success/latency per bucket. also sample bool for raw traces to keep cost down.

alex.h: here's a minimal policy sketch (for the console/backend config):
```
route: /v1/generate
canary: true
variants:
  - name: model-v2
    weight: 10
selection:
  strategy: consistent_hash
  key_priority: ["user_id","x-session-id","x-redwood-entropy"]
  hash_mod: 100
overrides:
  header: x-redwood-canary-override
  allowlist: [team-qa, partner-alpha]
```

taylor.p: looks good. UX notes: console should show an example mapping: "if you put user_id=12345 -> bucket 7 -> 10% -> model-v2" and a visual slider for percent + toggle for header allowlist. people get confused by backend-only configs.

maria.k: also add a preview tool to the console where you can paste a user_id/header and see which variant they'd hit (client-side preview). saves a ton of support noise.

jamal.r: operational risk: consistent-hash changes when variant set changes (e.g., adding model-v3). we need migration docs: either remap buckets or use a stable salt. add `deployment_salt` to policy to rotate intentionally.

alex.h: good point. add `salt` and show diff on console before apply.

sre-oncall: telemetry + alerting request: create a metric `canary_traffic_ratio(variant=*)` computed from routing.tags. alert if actual traffic deviates >5% from configured weight for >5min. also alert on error-rate-regression per bucket.

maria.k: one more: quotas. if we split by user_id, quotas per user must still apply. we should enforce per-customer quota after routing (so canary can't bypass quota). otherwise a partner in allowlist could eat capacity.

alex.h: yep enforce quotas post-routing. also need to ensure cache keys include variant if responses can differ. otherwise edge caches will serve wrong model outputs.

taylor.p: security: header override must be authenticated or only accepted from internal networks. don't let clients set `x-redwood-canary-override` from public endpoints.

jamal.r: implementation note: for consistent hashing we use xxhash64 on the key + salt, mod 100. super fast in C++ runtime. add audit logs whenever someone changes salt or weights.

alex.h: action items:
- jamal: implement hash selection + salt (bl) and expose telemetry tags (ETA 2w)
- maria: design console preview + slider + diff UI (ETA 1w)
- taylor: write docs for override allowlist + security guidelines (ETA 3d)
- sre-oncall: define alerts and dashboards query (ETA 4d)

maria.k: thanks — I'll mock the preview tomorrow and post screenshots here :eyes:

infra-bot: note: canary rollout will be bumped to 20% on 2025-10-13T02:00:00Z if health checks pass.

sre-oncall: noted. will watch dashboards. :eyes:
